subject: microbiology
title: Haemolytic Uraemic Syndrome, Lactose Fermentation and Klebsiella pneumoniae

steps.tx: **Haemolytic uraemic syndrome** is microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury after Shiga toxin diarrhoea (D plus HUS, peak age under five): toxin injures glomerular endothelium (Gb3 receptor rich), complement amplifies, supportive care and dialysis carry, eculizumab debated by severity, antibiotics and plasma products not routine.
steps.say: Bloody diarrhoea then pale, bruised and oliguric a week later: HUS timing.

right.title: HUS management
points: Early isotonic fluids during diarrhoea protective evidence
Long term renal and blood pressure follow up

steps.tx: **Shiga toxin mechanics** (AB5, B binding Gb3 globotriaosylceramide, A cutting 28S ribosomal RNA) halts endothelial protein synthesis, apoptosis and prothrombotic surfaces follow, Stx2 more HUS associated than Stx1, phage regulation linking antibiotics to toxin induction debates (SOS response). Gb3 distribution explains kidney and brain address.
steps.say: Gb3 postcode delivers toxin to glomerulus and brain; Stx2 carries the worse prognosis.

right.title: Amplifiers
points: Genetic regulator variants in atypical HUS separate

steps.tx: **Lactose fermentation** as bench clock: rapid fermenters (E coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter pink by 24 hours), late (Shigella sonnei, some Salmonella variants after days), non fermenters (Salmonella, Shigella, Proteus, Yersinia pale), MacConkey reading at the right hour separates stool pathogens from flora first pass.
steps.say: Pink by morning is flora thinking; pale colonies from dysentery earn workup.

left.title: Fermenter groups
points: Rapid: E coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Serratia

right.title: Reading discipline
points: Late fermentation on prolonged incubation noted
Mixed pink and pale sorted separately
Non lactose on TSI and panels confirmed

steps.tx: **Klebsiella pneumoniae** (Friedlander bacillus next lesson's heritage name) is a capsulated non motile lactose fermenter with mucoid colonies, causing lobar pneumonia in alcohol and diabetes (currant jelly sputum, upper lobe bulging fissures), urinary and liver abscess disease (hypermucoviscous K1 K2 with metastatic eye and CNS in Asia), and carbapenemase fame (KPC, NDM).
steps.say: Mucoid pink colonies plus currant jelly sputum: Klebsiella, with abscess and resistance sequels.

left.title: Klebsiella portrait
points: Heavy polysaccharide capsule, string test mucoviscosity

steps.tx: **Hypermucoviscous Klebsiella** (string test positive over 5 millimetres, regulators rmpA, capsule K1 K2, aerobactin) invades community livers and metastasises to eye and meninges in diabetics, distinguished from classical hospital strains, drainage plus ceftriaxone by susceptibility and eye vigilance mandatory in bacteraemia.
steps.say: String over five millimetres plus liver abscess: image the eyes and brain.

steps.tx: **Klebsiella bench kin** complete: oxytoca (indole positive, antibiotic diarrhoea), Rhinoscleromatis (rhinoscleroma granulomatous nose), ozaenae (atrophic rhinitis), Enterobacter cloacae complex (AmpC lesson), all lactose world citizens sorted by indole, motility, VP and panels. The distinction matters because a mucoid urinary isolate and a necrotising pneumonia isolate demand different urgency despite sharing a genus.
steps.say: Indole and motility sort the mucoid crowd in two moves.

steps.tx: **HUS differential** disciplines panic: atypical complement mediated HUS (no diarrhoea, eculizumab), TTP (ADAMTS13, neurology, plasma exchange), pneumococcal HUS (T antigen), DIC and malignant hypertension, each with first tests (ADAMTS13, complement, Coombs) before attributing to last week's diarrhoea. ADAMTS13 activity below ten percent strongly supports TTP, whereas modest reductions occur in many inflammatory states and should not delay plasma exchange when suspicion is high.
steps.say: Schistocytes plus low platelets is a syndrome, not a diagnosis: prodrome separates STEC from TTP.

right.title: HUS mimics
points: TTP: severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, plasma exchange urgent

steps.tx: **Outbreak control in STEC** (food traceback, person to person in childcare (low dose), exclusion of cases from food and care work until clearance by jurisdiction, swimming and farm visit tracing) extends HUS prevention beyond hospital to the food chain that seeded it.
steps.say: One child's HUS audits a burger chain, a petting farm and a nursery register.

left.title: Investigation
points: Ground beef, unpasteurised and produce vehicles

right.title: Exclusions
points: Food handlers and childcare until cleared
Stool clearance rules by risk group
